# Draft:Battle of Maltokri and Khalifan

Kurdistan Democratic Party (PDK) / Peshmerga

The Battle of Maltokri and Khalifan took place in August 1965 during the Aylul Revolution in the Ruandz region of Kurdistan. It was a coordinated effort by the Kurdish Peshmerga forces to capture strategic mountain positions and military bases controlled by the Iraqi Army.
Background
The Iraqi government intensified its military pressure on Kurdish regions, targeting key locations such as Ruandz, Mount Korek, and the Diyana Plain. In response, the Kurdish revolutionary leadership, led by Mustafa Barzani, organized a comprehensive offensive to secure strategic high ground and disrupt Iraqi Army positions.
Battle
The offensive began on August 6, 1965, with coordinated artillery bombardments on Iraqi bases at Khalifan, Maltokri, Ruandz, Hamiya, Kawlokan, and Diyana. Peshmerga forces, led by commanders including Mullah Amin, Hamaziad, and Lieutenant Riaz Badrkhan, launched simultaneous assaults on Mount Korek and surrounding military positions. The Maltokri base was seized by Balak forces under Ezzat Sulaiman Beg Dargalayi and Mam Sdiq, while the Khalifan and Diyana bases were heavily attacked by other Peshmerga units. Despite the destruction of several barracks and artillery success, some key positions, including the Kapka Qalawi outpost on Mount Korek, resisted capture due to difficult terrain and determined Iraqi defense led by Major Qahtan.
Outcome
While the primary strategic objectives were not fully achieved, the operation inflicted significant damage on Iraqi military infrastructure. The Peshmerga suffered casualties, including 27 fighters killed on the Korek front, but successfully captured and destroyed several Iraqi outposts and barracks. The battle demonstrated the coordination and resilience of the Kurdish revolutionary forces against a numerically and technologically superior enemy. Following the battle, the Peshmerga fortified their defensive lines in anticipation of further Iraqi counterattacks.
